lines.text: choose the hero on purpose, not an attractor: a glowing circle or orb, a dusk sun or crescent, a light-poetry name like Vesper
pick one thread that carries through (an object, a type line, a colour or a rhythm), not separate reveals one after another
draw three directions from different materials (type, paper, liquid, cut geometry, photograph, UI, light), not three colours of one idea; at most one is light

more.text: name the act that causes each change ("the cursor hits Send on the card"), not "then" or "it cuts to"
give each beat a role, a persuasion move and a feeling arc, and cut a beat with none, not a beat kept for filler
show on screen every claim the copy makes in the same beat, or cut it, not "26 looks" with fewer than 26 on screen
enlarge, lengthen or cut an effect the viewer cannot see at its real size and time, not a glow on dark content or a 0.4 s blinds wipe
write the motion register in the brief before the restraint level, not a hype film where every beat moves the same way
name three ways to do each beat and reject the first, not rise plus fade as the default
map each piece of product material to a beat and leave out what maps to none, not every fact in the film
follow the font, type size, UI scale and camera the film declares in DESIGN.md under "## Declared", not a house default
show a real artifact working in each beat (the real UI or the brand's own world), not a word in a box
take the reference's style (grammar, light, type, moves) and rebuild it with your own subject, not its text, logos or photos
embed only assets you may publish and capture the real product UI, not copyrighted posters, stills, news photos or music
take the theme from the brand site, ask when the prompt is bare, and invent one on purpose for "you choose", not plain grey
pick one visual style as the register and justify it from the brand's own site, not a mix of styles
use only CC0 or CC BY music you can show a licence for and log it in assets/music/credits.json, not CC ND or CC NC

lines.text: keep the accent on one thing, not a full-frame flood
show the subject by 0.1 s, not an empty ground for the first half second
put soft colour blobs behind the content, not one flat fill
give each frame one focal point and one accent colour, not two things fighting
read the brand CSS tokens and tint the neutrals, not pure #000, #fff or a guessed palette

set a read line at a 6% cap height (UI that is the subject, in data-ui: 3%) and hold it 0.6 s a word from 4 words (a 4 word tagline 2.4 s), fewer words max(1.2 s, words/3), not a small tagline that flashes by
use the kit's face and ground or a face the direction chose, not Inter or Space Grotesk by habit
colour one or two words per line, each the word the beat is about, not every word

more.text: use a comma, a period or a middle dot in on-screen text, not an em dash
pick the layout by what the beat does and change three or more of layout, scale, value, ground, hue and motion between neighbours, not the same archetype twice
compose asymmetric with one hero anchored to an edge or a third, not a centred 6/6 split
give a graphic that carries a beat at least 8 percent of the canvas and demote the type to a caption, not a mark-sized graphic
turn the ground to a second hue family from the palette in two or more worlds, not three shots within a 40 degree hue span
pair the hero claim with a smaller proof in any beat held over 3 s, with 2 to 5 decoratives, not a big word centred on empty space
make one element dominant by scale (hero 60 to 80 percent of the width, small caption) and soften the support, not three medium lines
show a company's mark whenever it is named and keep one icon family, not a text-only list of named things
use the lightest visual that carries the meaning, a clean gradient before a photo, not an image on a beat that reads fine on a plain field
treat each image by its job with the lightest treatment that works, not a raw flat screenshot or an over-graded one
size the logo mark at 5 percent of the frame height or more, with real weight on the end card, not a logo as punctuation
draw bloom, fringe, focus and flares with the lens surface, not a CSS blur or radial gradient that imitates one
keep essential content inside the inner 90 percent of the frame, checked on the real box after layout, not in the margin
snap text blocks to at most three left edges in one frame, not a new edge for each block
lock a bespoke surface in one page of tokens before you author it and check the frame against it, not a silent swap of palette, family or radius
set a headline on a flat patch with 3:1 contrast for large text and 4.5:1 for body, not on a moving blob or gradient hot spot
use three text sizes (hero, support, label) with at most six in a frame, not many near sizes
set display type tight (letter-spacing -0.03em) and body type open at a 45 to 75 character measure, not one tracking for both
use one to three faces, each with a role, and recolour at the same weight to emphasise, not a heavier bold or a second expressive face
follow the brand hero's value, light site light-first and dark site dark-first, with 2 px or heavier borders on light, not a swapped dark design
use the full 100 to 900 weight range for hierarchy, light against black, not size alone or thin weights that shimmer
name what each empty area does in one clause, and enlarge the subject when the gap is passive, not a leftover gap between two things

lines.text: hold a line of 4 or more words 0.6 s per word once settled (a 4 word line 2.4 s), fewer words max(1.2 s, words / 3), and take it off when read plus 1.5 s, not hold it for the beat
leave beats with no words, not text in every frame
turn the world every 4 to 6 s (a new element, a cut, a ground swap), not one lockup held
cut, wipe on the motion or match a shape, not a muddy crossfade
land the next subject where the eye was (within 0.3 of the frame diagonal), not across the frame
change axis or direction at every moving seam, not the same seam move twice

more.text: make the CTA the shortest scene, 3 to 5 s with one action, and keep the world moving under it, not a faded or frozen end card
pose the question in the first 3 s (at most 12 words) and show the payoff late, from 77 percent of the runtime, not the best fact in the hook
size the scene count to the runtime (5 to 7 scenes in 30 s) and vary scene length, 3 to 7 s, not equal scenes
alternate punchy shots (0.8 to 1.5 s) with breathing shots (2 to 3 s), and keep a clip 1.2 s or longer, not one cut length
fly the camera through one space at constant speed on interior legs and ease only at the ends, not an eased stop at every waypoint
cut on the beat or two frames early on a completed action, not in a dead hold
cover a ground jump (dark to light) with a colour that peaks at the cut, not a full-bleed fade-out flash
make the hard cut the default seam and earn 2 to 3 transition accents by meaning, not a transition on every seam
align the two silhouettes before a match cut, not a match cut with no real rhyme
pair each directional entrance with an exit that continues the same line of travel, not an element that enters and retreats
give each seam a reason (relationship and feeling across it) or use a hard cut, not "it looks smoother"
time each seam by its type (whip 0.27 to 0.4 s, slide 0.5 to 1 s, fade 0.66 to 1.33 s) and end the outgoing text at the seam, not a double blend

lines.text: land an entrance on EASE.land with most of the move shown by frame 1, not a slow-start ease-in or a scale(0) start
make each entrance a move with an origin, not everything fading in
exit shorter than the entrance on EASE.launch, not an exit as long as its entrance
keep one part moving in every hold (typing, a counter, glint() or breathe() from core/motion/alive.js), not a frozen frame and not a camera drift
take curves from EASE names (or a sampled spring), not a CSS keyword or a hand-fitted cubic-bezier
land about 1 in 3 arrivals with a spring (EASE.pop), not every arrival on one soft stop, and never a spring on a count
sample a spring or exponential with 8 or more stops, not one cubic-bezier sold as physics
put each move in a speed band with the slowest move 3x the fastest and the fastest under 12 frame heights a second, not every move at one duration
stagger a group 30 to 80 ms, not a group that lands on one frame

more.text: give a hero move a small opposite wind-up (2 to 4 percent dip), not an anticipation on every move
start the next move while the last still settles, even steps in a cascade and irregular for different things, not a metronome
blur only what moves fast and echo the glyph outline for type, not a blurred still
blur out and fade faces, cards and dense grids on exit, not a slide of many elements at once
put each effect on the frame after its cause (press, then the answer; the sound on its own action), not before it
hold the camera still and give the hold an element motion, moving it for at most 60 percent of the film and 4 worlds in a row, not a drift on every beat
finish a trailing property 0.05 to 0.15 s after the main one (scale after position, shadow after card), not everything ending on one frame
let one element own the motion of a beat and the rest support quietly, one claim per element, not rise plus rotate on one object
give the spectacle second the fastest or longest move of the film, with quiet before it, not a stronger peak elsewhere
run audio across a picture change with a 0.35 s equal-power crossfade, not two sounds butted together

lines.text: keep gradients clean with 1 to 2% grain, not banding rings or a straight seam in a glow
let every mark ride its parent, not a mark that points at nothing
end on motion in the last 1 s, not a frozen lockup
use a stock device (sheen band, lens streak, light beam, accent bar, rule line) once, not as the idea
pad each reveal mask 0.3 em past the glyphs, not letters cut by their own reveal
tie each cue to one visible event and cue the first and the last key word, not a tick on every word
keep the true peak at or below -3 dBFS and the mix near -20 LUFS, not a mix pushed loud
take a recorded effect first (resources/README.md), not a synth bed or a tick on every cut
